units.title: Backward interpolation yields gradient contraction
units.statement: Let P_u be positive real-linear evolution operators and q_u a family of observables. If α>0, the expanded CD(α,∞) inequality holds, Φ(u)=P_uΓ(q_u) is continuous, and its exact right derivative is P_u(LΓ(q_u)−2Γ(q_u,Lq_u)), then Φ(s)≤Φ(t)e^{-2α(t-s)} for s≤t.
assumptions: X is arbitrary and L is real-linear on real-valued observables.
The curvature parameter α is strictly positive and the fully expanded diagonal CD inequality holds for every observable and point.
Each P_u is real-linear and preserves pointwise order.
The scalar interpolation Φ(u)=P_uΓ(q_u)(x) is continuous.
At every u, its exact right derivative within [u,∞) is P_u(LΓ(q_u)−2Γ(q_u,Lq_u))(x).

steps.title: Turn curvature into a pointwise generator bound
steps.text: The expanded CD inequality gives LΓ(q_u)−2Γ(q_u,Lq_u)≥2αΓ(q_u) at every state.

steps.title: Push the inequality through the positive linear evolution
steps.text: Order preservation maps the pointwise bound through P_u; linearity pulls out 2α. The supplied derivative identity then gives Φ'(u)≥2αΦ(u).
steps.lean: Use hpositive, then simplify with the linear-map laws.

steps.title: Read the backward interpolation endpoints
steps.text: The scalar comparison theorem converts the derivative lower bound into exponential contraction from t back to s.

units.lean_statement: Every curvature, positivity, continuity, derivative, and endpoint premise is explicit. The evolution and orbit are arbitrary functions of real time; no semigroup law is inferred.
units.lean_proof: The proof derives the pointwise curvature bound, transfers it through each positive linear operator, and invokes the independently verified scalar backward interpolation theorem.
units.boundary: The theorem assumes rather than proves the exact derivative identity, positivity, continuity, and domain closure for a concrete semigroup. It does not construct a diffusion or identify a concrete generator.
